content.title: About
content.content: Flour tortilla is a thin, flexible flatbread made from wheat flour, water, salt, and sometimes a small amount of fat. It is a staple of Mexican cuisine, used for tacos, burritos, quesadillas and many other dishes. The dough is rolled into round discs and quickly cooked on a dry skillet or grill.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat tortillas originated in the northern regions of Mexico where wheat grew better than corn.
Compared with corn tortillas, wheat versions are softer and more pliable, making them ideal for wrapping fillings.
Traditionally tortillas were hand‑rolled on a stone surface called a “tacita”.
In the United States wheat tortillas became popular in the 1920s thanks to Mexican restaurants and fast‑food chains.
Tortillas can be kept in the refrigerator for up to a week and frozen for up to three months.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Tortillas provide a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Wheat flour in tortillas adds fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: Tortillas contain thiamine, niacin and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When cooked without added oil, tortillas have a modest fat content.

items.title: Convenient way to add vegetables
items.content: Tortillas make it easy to incorporate vegetables, beans and lean proteins into meals.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat tortillas contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because the carbs are rapidly absorbed, tortillas can raise blood sugar levels, which is relevant for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some commercial tortillas contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tortillas as a base for tacos, burritos, quesadillas, fajitas and wraps. Heat them on a dry skillet, in the microwave or in the oven. Thin tortillas work well for rolls, while thicker ones are good for baked dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store tortillas in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 5 days. For longer storage keep them refrigerated for up to 2 weeks or frozen for up to 3 months. Warm before use to restore flexibility.
